provenance: Found while pinning `cover-refusal-envelope`, 2026-08-24 -- the defect the refusal fix EXPOSED rather than caused. MEASURED RED once the refusal path carried the key: registrant_name resolved to '---------------' at 0.95 via `caption_anchored`. ksb-2007 is a fixed-width .txt cover that UNDERLINES each value with a rule -- '24HOLDINGS INC.\n---------------\n(EXACT NAME OF REGISTRANT AS SPECIFIED IN ITS CHARTER)' -- so orientation A's 'the line above the caption' is the rule, not the value. The first draft of this case asserted `missing`, which was WRONG and is recorded here rather than quietly corrected: the author read the envelope's SGML wrapper ('-----BEGIN PRIVACY-ENHANCED MESSAGE-----') and concluded the filing had no cover at all, when it has a perfectly ordinary one 2,000 characters further in. The rule that fixes it is that a name -- and a state -- contains LETTERS, applied to all three caption orientations and the positional fallback at once, because the underline shape is a .txt-era convention and not a property of refused documents. This filing is a 10-KSB and is refused, so the case also proves the refusal envelope's cover is resolved over the real cover region and not over the wrapper.
